sources.locator: Delegates in Tucumán declared independence of the United Provinces in 1816 after the 1810 revolution. Original Spanish preamble, 1853 constitution with 1994 amendments and continuing federal republican framework. The so-called Conquest of the Desert was a violent culmination of long relations among Indigenous peoples, settlers and the Argentine state, not conquest of empty land. State-approved military campaigns across Patagonia 1878–85, including 1879 Río Negro expedition. 1884 law established common, free, compulsory, gradual primary education. Tango developed among urban lower classes in Buenos Aires and Montevideo through European, African-descended and criollo cultural exchange. Yerba mate has Guaraní roots; people share a gourd and bombilla in rounds, with one person preparing and serving, though customs vary. Archive preserves evidence of human-rights crimes in 1976–83 military dictatorship and reparations. 1983 election restored democratic civilian government after the 1976 military dictatorship.

sources.locator: Seven-province Republic and the States General through 1795. Former commercial power invested wealth in houses, interiors and portraits; eighteenth-century gallery. 1747 image commemorates William IV becoming stadtholder. Fourth Anglo-Dutch War 1780 to 1784 brought naval, economic and political crisis. Patriots and French troops ended the old republic in 1795; 1798 constitution and original Dutch text; equality excluded women and enslaved people. VOC carried coffee, tea, spices and textiles from Asia; held military power and used violence and slavery. Dutch planters expanded Suriname plantations using forced labor of enslaved Africans. Smallpox threatened eighteenth-century Amsterdam children; cowpox vaccination arrived around 1800.

Rejewski and Polish Cipher Bureau colleagues deciphered Enigma; Polish intelligence passed methods to British and French counterparts in July 1939. 1980 Gdańsk Shipyard strike, Anna Walentynowicz, support from families bringing food and medicine, underground print culture and independent Solidarity trade union. Article 1 original Polish wording; constitution defines the democratic state and citizens’ rights.

sources.locator: The Crown established a viceroyalty in 1535 after the 1521 conquest; Indigenous communities faced epidemics, coerced labor and imposed institutions but persisted. In 1535 the viceroyalty governed Mexico, Guatemala, the Caribbean, Florida and southwestern North America from Mexico City. Colonial legal records cover New Spain and later Mexican states, with historical jurisdiction extending well beyond modern Mexico. Sixteenth-century epidemic diseases devastated Native communities and disrupted their societies. In 1571 Indigenous Nahuatl officials used a pictorial legal record to complain of mistreatment and underpayment. Nahua students wrote Nahuatl in Latin letters and painted illustrations; a Spanish translation stands beside their text. Silver left New Spain for Asian goods; silk and porcelain came to Acapulco and influenced Mexican arts. Mexico achieved independence in 1821 and inherited most but not all of the viceroyalty; the Philippines and Caribbean were not part of independent Mexico.
